items.stem: Why write a precise problem statement before generating solutions?

options.text: It focuses analysis on the real problem and prevents solving the wrong thing
options.rationale: Correct: a sharp problem statement aligns effort on the actual issue and its success criteria.

options.text: It guarantees the first solution considered will be correct
options.rationale: A statement frames the problem; it does not guarantee a first-try solution.

options.text: It removes any need to gather evidence
options.rationale: Evidence gathering is still required after framing.

options.text: It is only useful for documentation after the fact
options.rationale: The statement guides the whole analysis, not just documentation.

items.explanation: Correct: a sharp problem statement aligns effort on the actual issue and its success criteria.

items.stem: Which statements about structuring a problem with an issue tree are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Branches should be mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE)
options.rationale: Correct: MECE branches avoid overlap and gaps, making the analysis complete and clean.

options.text: Each branch can be turned into a testable hypothesis
options.rationale: Correct: issue-tree branches translate into hypotheses that evidence can confirm or reject.

options.text: Overlapping branches make the analysis clearer
options.rationale: Overlap causes double-counting and confusion; MECE avoids it.

options.text: An issue tree should list only the solution, not the drivers
options.rationale: An issue tree decomposes drivers of the problem, not just a chosen solution.

items.explanation: Correct: MECE branches avoid overlap and gaps, making the analysis complete and clean.; Correct: issue-tree branches translate into hypotheses that evidence can confirm or reject.

items.stem: A team fixes the first cause they find, but the problem recurs. What technique most directly addresses this?

options.text: Five whys, to keep asking why past the first cause until the root cause is reached
options.rationale: Correct: five whys drives past surface causes to the underlying root cause.

options.text: Choosing the first option generated to save time
options.rationale: That is a cause of the problem, not a remedy.

options.text: Skipping evidence gathering to move faster
options.rationale: Skipping evidence makes recurrence more likely, not less.

options.text: Broadening the problem statement until it is vague

items.explanation: Correct: five whys drives past surface causes to the underlying root cause.
